_what: The places on this computer the person shares with their AIs, and the person's hold on them (tools/drive-the-screen/read-data/work-places.mjs is blind; every place and every word is here). A kind with `singleton` exists without being made. `person_input` on a kind means the person's own keyboard and pointer reach that place: their last input, read by the top-level `person_input` row, holds the place for `limits.idle_ttl_ms` (input the AI's own action made, within `limits.acted_slack_ms` of it, is not theirs). The person takes a place over for at most `limits.longest_take_over_minutes` and hands it back with the key given at take over; `file` keeps the holds and `folder` the person's hand-back keys.

person_input._what: The Mac's own count of how long since the last keyboard or pointer input (nanoseconds), read without any permission.

words.kept_file: The places file could not be read, so nothing was changed: {error}
words.not_taken: Nobody has taken over {place}; it is already the AIs'.
words.person_has_it: The person took over {place} at {since} and has it until {until}. Do not act there until they hand it back; look at it if you need to.
words.person_using_it: The person is using {place} right now (their last input was {seconds} seconds ago). Wait until they have left it alone for {ttl} seconds.
words.taken_over: You have {place} until {until}. Your AIs are refused there until you hand it back.
words.told_handed_back: The person had {place} from {since} to {until} and handed it back{note}. Look at it again before you act.
words.unknown_place: There is no place called {place} on this computer. The places are: {places}.
words.wrong_key: That is not the key the person was given when they took over {place}.
